title: Surgical canary neutralization and multi-plane fixplay for tenant escalations
text:
Surgical canary neutralization and multi-plane fixplay for tenant escalations

description:
Urgent runbook and automation to neutralize a problematic canary slice that is causing customer-facing regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to create a low-latency, tenant-aware procedure for: (1) fast isolation of affected tenants, (2) safe KV-cache and prefix cache reconciliation, (3) coordinated model pin/rollforward/rollback across control planes, and (4) a clear customer communication pathway tied to severity and SLA. This ticket captures the playbook, automated scripts, comms templates, and short-term hotfix steps plus a follow-up engineering project for permanent mitigations (better routing policies, quicker cache invalidation hooks, and rollback automation).

acceptance_criteria:
A1: Runbook executed end-to-end in staging with synthetic tenant slices and no data leak between slices
A2: Automation can fence an affected tenant in <= 90s and revert traffic routing to a pinned model variant within 3 minutes
A3: KV prefix invalidation workflow completes within SLO (<= 2 minutes) for both Hosted and Dedicated controllers
A4: Customer communication templates are approved by Support and Legal and available for immediate use
A5: Postmortem checklist and owners assigned for follow-up fixes included in runtime-1.23 planning

playbook_steps:
Detection: Alert triggers via SLO delta (latency + quality alerts) and templated query to slice by tenant tags in tracing dashboard (Grafana: /d/slo/tenant-slices)
Triage: Triage lead (oncall) runs synthetic prompt set against canary variant to verify regression; record failing prompts in a secure incident doc
Isolate: Use routing API to redirect the tenant's traffic to degraded-safe path: 'safety-proxy' tier or smaller-capacity fallback variant; mark tenant as 'fenced' in ticketing
Pin & Rollback: If regression is model-quality related, pin the tenant to the previous stable model variant (model-id field) in control plane; if binary bug, roll forward hotfix via canary patch pipeline
KV Cache Reconciliation: Trigger KV-drain and prefix invalidation for affected host shards. Run 'tools/kvcache/reconcile --slice <slice_id> --fast' and monitor eviction logs
Session/Prefix Rehydration: If prefix cache invalidation causes cold-start errors, enable staged rehydration against a warm replica controlled by the rehydration orchestrator
Cross-Plane Coordination: Notify Dedicated and Private plane owners via escalation channel and execute plane-specific fencing commands (see plane playbook links)
Customer Comms: Use canned templates (Support/Legal approved) to notify customers within SLA; escalate to AE for high-revenue tenants
Observation: Monitor token-level latency, generation quality metrics, and error rates for 30 minutes post-action. Keep CS updated every 10 minutes for P0s
Rollback Confirmation & Cleanup: After stability window, remove fencing flags, reconcile caches again, and run post-check scripts to ensure no stale KV artifacts remain

decision_log:
D1: Opted for tenant fencing + model pinning as first-line mitigation rather than global rollback to avoid broad customer impact
D2: Prioritized fast KV prefix invalidation (even if it causes temporary cold starts) because silent stale KV artifacts have historically caused repeat regressions
D3: Decided to require Support + Legal signoff on outbound comms for P0 escalations involving private deployments with contractual SLAs
D4: Chose to implement an automated 'canary-neutralize' script in runtime manager rather than a purely manual checklist to reduce mean-time-to-isolate

recent_updates:
2026-03-10: Created ticket after oncall escalated a P0 canary regression affecting 3 hosted tenants and 1 dedicated tenant. Initial triage confirmed model quality drop (BLEU and API-level hallucination increase).
2026-03-11: Daniel deployed 'canary-neutralize' v0.1 to staging; ran synthetic slice test and observed KV drain completing in 45s on staging nodes.
2026-03-12: Support drafted customer notice; Legal requested additional wording for private deployments. Template updated and approved 2026-03-13.
2026-03-13: Hotfix branch opened in runtime (PR #4821) implementing automated model pin handshake. Guardrails added to require two approvers for canary neutralize in prod.
2026-03-14: Performed a smoke run in a dedicated capacity sandbox using tenant-slice replay; fencing + pinning sequence completed in 88s end-to-end. Observability: latency spike during rehydration but errors stayed within acceptable thresholds.

next_actions:
Action 1: Merge PR #4821 after a second approver reviews and schedule blue/green release to dedicated staging on 2026-03-16
Action 2: Implement alert enrichment to include slice_id and last-successful-model in telemetry within 2 sprints
Action 3: Add 'canary-neutralize' to oncall runbook and run a tabletop with SRE, Support, and Solutions Engineering on 2026-03-18
Action 4: Create a follow-up project to harden routing policies and add atomic prefix-invalidation primitives for runtime-1.23
